coTenancy.verbatimQuote: An Exempted Discontinuance shall mean the closure of a tenant's store because of casualty, condemnation, repairs or remodeling for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days. A tenant's store which is closed due to an Exempted Discontinuance shall not be considered closed for purposes of determining whether a Secondary Reduced Occupancy Period is in effect (and the Leasable Floor Area of such tenant's store shall not be calculated in the numerator or the denominator of the fraction specified in Section 1.7.2) from the commencement of the Exempted Discontinuance until the earlier of: the expiration of such ninety (90) day period; or (ii) the expiration of the Exempted Discontinuance. For more information, refer to Article 6.1.3.

keyAssumptions: Source: JLL Offering Memorandum 'Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio' (99 pp., undated; cash flow 1/1/2027-12/31/2037). This property: overview PDF p.6, site plan p.7, trade area p.8, assumptions/opex p.9, RE taxes p.10-11, rent roll pp.12-20, cash flow p.21.
TIE-OUT (verified by script): roster SF 625,453 = OM GLA 625,453; occupied 575,582 SF + vacant 49,871 SF; occupancy 92.0% (OM states 96%).
TIE-OUT: in-place base rent on the roster $11,878,411 vs OM rent-roll total $12,174,463; JLL Year-1 EGR $14,710,102 - OpEx $4,130,134 = NOI $10,579,968 (matches the portfolio summary, p.1).
TIE-OUT: 16 tax parcel(s) on the OM tax page sum to $1,637,684 vs the cash-flow RE tax line $1,637,685 (2026 assessment x millage grown 3%, net of 2% discount where shown).
WALT 4.9 yrs computed SF-weighted from lease expiries as of 1/1/2027 (OM states 5.1); weighted-avg base rent $20.64/SF over rent-paying occupied SF.
NO asking price or cap rate is disclosed (portfolio is marketed unpriced) - both left null.

JLL leasing assumptions: 75% renewal probability, 12 months downtime, $30/SF TI new / $0 renewal, 6%/3% LCs, 5% general vacancy (excluding credit/anchor tenants), 3% management fee, $0.20/SF reserves.

Lease-clause detail (co-tenancy, exclusives, termination/go-dark, ROFR) comes from the seller's summary workbook 'Midwest & Midatlantic Portfolio - Exclusives, Co-Tenancy, Restrictions.xlsx' - a summary, NOT the executed leases; every clause is marked unverified.
Rent roll as-of: the OM's cash flow starts 1/1/2027 (JLL's assumed closing); tenantsAsOf is set to that date by convention, not an observation date.

Corrected occupancy: 575,582 SF occupied / 625,453 SF = 92.0%. The OM's 96% (600,253 'leased') counts the 24,671 SF Speculative Tenant; the only truly 'Available' suite in the OM is Phase II-127 (25,200 SF).
Base rent: $12,174,463 OM roll total (ties to the PDF p.20 footer and the Yr-1 Scheduled Base Rent of $12,174,460); $11,878,411 excluding the speculative tenant.
Other income: St. Margaret's easement $45,000/yr (rising to $50,000 in 2030).
Ground rent $494,434 sits in operating expenses above NOI (JLL proforma); management fee 3% of EGR; capital reserves $0.20/SF below NOI.

Giant Eagle sales: OM states $92,960,678 (p.6); the Gumberg sales report's CY2024 figure ($142.5M) includes catch-up postings for months missing from CY2023 and was NOT used; the last clean year is CY2022 at $89.6M ($828/SF).

Tenant sales from the Gumberg 'Gross Sales History' report (Dec-2024 run; both files 'Pages 1-80' and 'Pages 81-138 from All Property Sales.pdf'); only full 12-month (or annual-filer) years are used - partial/catch-up years are skipped. Sales PSF uses the OM rent-roll SF.
deals.notes: **Waterworks** is a **625,453 SF Giant Eagle Market District-anchored power center** on Freeport Road at the edge of Fox Chapel/Aspinwall, inside Pittsburgh city limits - the dominant center in its trade area (#1 most-visited within 15 miles, **6.1M visits** L12M) with **$108,916 AHHI and 85,018 people within 3 miles**. Giant Eagle (108,151 SF, $13.34/SF) does **$92.96M ($860/SF)** for a 1.6% rent-to-sales ratio, and the box lineup is deep credit: Dick's (55,000 SF, new 2025 lease to 2036), HomeGoods, T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, Ross, Barnes & Noble, Ulta, Five Below and Petco, plus a 33,168 SF cinema (rent ~21% of its 2023 sales, and 2024 sales slipping) and 10 bank/QSR pads paying $30-$105/SF. JLL's Year-1 NOI is **$10,579,968**, but it counts a 24,671 SF **'Speculative Tenant' with no lease** at $12.00/SF as occupied - carried here as vacant, **true occupancy is 92.0% (not 96%)** and in-place NOI is ~$10.29M. The defining risk is the **2028 rollover: $3.52M of base rent (30%) and 228,451 SF expire in calendar 2028** - Giant Eagle (8/2028), T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, Ross and Barnes & Noble (all 1/2028) - although nearly all carry fixed-rate options and the sales support them (T.J. Maxx $343/SF at 3.8% rent-to-sales). The landlord also pays **$494,434/yr of ground rent to Kroger** for a parcel under the center (stepping to $531,517 in 2032), a leasehold component that must be diligenced. Thesis: an irreplaceable, high-income infill power center bought for durable cash flow and modest growth (JLL Yr1-6 NOI CAGR 2.2%), with real upside in leasing the 49,871 SF of Phase II/III vacancy; the price has to reflect the 2028 renewal wall and the Walmart-era co-tenancy clauses in Phase I. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: An **irreplaceable Fox Chapel-edge power center** with a **$92.96M Giant Eagle** and deep credit boxes, held back by **30% of base rent rolling in 2028**, a **Kroger ground lease** and an OM occupancy that **counts a speculative tenant** (true occupancy 92.0%).
strengths: Giant Eagle Market District does $92.96M ($860/SF) - 1.6% rent-to-sales - and is the #1-visited grocer within 5 miles; renewal at $14.67/SF in 2028 is highly likely.
Affluent infill trade area: $108,916 AHHI and 85,018 people within 3 miles, 267,492 within 5; 6.1M annual visits (95th percentile nationally).
Deep national box lineup (Dick's to 2036, HomeGoods, T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, Ross, Ulta, Five Below, Barnes & Noble, Petco) plus 10 bank/QSR pads.

Strong sales where reported: Marshalls $322/SF and T.J. Maxx $343/SF (~4% rent-to-sales), Bath & Body Works $685, Chipotle $1,455, Mad Mex $719, Five Guys $660, Aladdin's $552, Pearle $548, Ichiban $515 - most in-line tenants at 4-9% rent-to-sales.
All 9 OM figures tie out: roster SF 625,453 = GLA, base rent $12,174,463 = roll total, 16 tax parcels sum to the $1,637,685 cash-flow tax line.
risks: 2028 rollover wall: Giant Eagle, T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, Ross, Barnes & Noble and six in-line tenants - 228,451 SF / $3.52M (30% of base rent).
OM's 96% occupancy and $10.58M NOI include a 24,671 SF 'Speculative Tenant' with no lease ($296,052 of rent); true occupancy 92.0%.
$494,434/yr ground rent to Kroger (rising to $531,517 in 2032) - a leasehold position under part of the center.
Phase I co-tenancy clauses (Anytime Fitness, Hallmark, Sally Beauty) are keyed to a Walmart that is no longer on the roll - status must be confirmed.
Weak occupancy-cost tenants: GNC (21.6% base rent-to-sales), Cold Stone (17.1%), Petco (14.9%, no options, 1/2031), Barnes & Noble (13.9% on 2022 sales), Blume Nails ($56/SF reported).
Waterworks Cinemas: $669,220 of rent (no options, to 12/2035) against $3.22M of 2023 sales (20.8%), with Jan-Oct 2024 down ~23% year over year.

upsideItems.item: Lease the 49,871 SF of Phase II/III vacancy
upsideItems.detail: Phase II-127 (25,200 SF, JLL market $14.00/SF in the >25k band) and Phase III-02 (24,671 SF, JLL's spec deal at $12.00/SF) - roughly $650k of base rent at JLL's assumptions, ~6% on top of in-place NOI, before recoveries.
Giant Eagle's first option steps rent from $13.34 to $14.67/SF (+$143,800/yr) in 9/2028; at $860/SF sales the renewal is the most certain growth in the deal.

Ten separately-parcelled pads (PNC $93.66/SF, Citizens $104.82, Keybank $86.60, Bank of America $69.39, McDonald's, Wendy's, Chili's, Eat'n Park, Taco Bell, Dollar Bank) are on their own tax parcels - a pad-sale program could harvest low-cap STNL pricing. Check REA/ground-lease restrictions first.

redFlags.description: 2028 ROLLOVER WALL - $3,517,576 of base rent (30%) and 228,451 SF expire in 2028: Giant Eagle 8/31/2028 (108,151 SF), T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, Ross and Barnes & Noble all 1/31/2028, plus Top Hat, Philip Pelusi, Cold Stone, Mad Mex, Uncle Sam's and GNC. Most hold fixed options (GE three 5-yr at $14.67/$16.14/$17.76; OM also notes 'at FMV'), so this is a renewal-negotiation window rather than a vacancy cliff - but it lands in Year 2 of any hold.

OCCUPANCY/NOI OVERSTATED BY A SPECULATIVE TENANT - the OM rent roll (PDF p.20) carries 'Speculative Tenant' in Phase III-02 (24,671 SF) at $12.00/SF ($296,052/yr) 'assumed in-place at the analysis start'. No lease exists. Corrected occupancy is 92.0% (not 96%) and in-place NOI is roughly $10.29M before that space's recoveries.

GROUND LEASE - the landlord pays Kroger ~$494,434/yr for a parcel under the center (OM p.9 footnote 4: 'Contact JLL for more detail'), stepping to $531,517 in 2032. Term, renewal rights, rent resets and what improvements sit on the Kroger land are undisclosed - get the ground lease before bidding.

WALMART-KEYED CO-TENANCY IN PHASE I - Anytime Fitness (50% rent or termination), Hallmark (12%-of-sales substitute rent / termination) and Sally Beauty (termination) all name Walmart, which is not on the current roll. Whether those prongs were satisfied by replacement tenants or are already failing is not stated in the seller's summary - confirm via estoppels.

CINEMA RENT BURDEN - Waterworks Cinemas (33,168 SF, $669,220 = 6% of base rent, $20.18/SF stepping to $21.56 in 11/2027 and $23.22 in 11/2032, NO options, lease to 12/31/2035) reported $3,219,211 of sales in CY2023 - base rent is 20.8% of sales before recoveries - and Jan-Oct 2024 sales ran $2.11M vs $2.72M for the same months of 2023 (-23%). Screen count is not disclosed, so sales per screen can't be computed. Rent at this level is a rent-relief / go-dark candidate; get the operator's full-year 2024-25 sales.

SELLER LEASE SUMMARIES COVER PHASE I ONLY - the clause workbook's Waterworks tab is 'Waterworks I'; no co-tenancy/exclusive/termination summaries were provided for Phase II/III (Giant Eagle, T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods, Ulta, Five Below, Dick's, the cinema). Ross's own occupancy co-tenancy threshold (Lease Art. 6.1.3) is also not reproduced.

coTenancy.verbatimQuote: "Anchor Tenant" shall mean the Other Required Lessee or a tenant which (a) on a regional or national basis, operates under the same trade name at least ten (10) high quality retail stores comparably sized to the respective Anchor Premises, in a manner which is consistent with a first class promotional shopping center in the Pittsburgh Metropolitan area, and (b) operates as one of the following: (i) full line department store, (ii) junior department store, (iii) soft good store, (iv) supermarket, (v) sporting good store, (vi) home improvements store, (vii) catalog store, (viii) drug store, (ix) toy superstore, (x) electronic equipment/appliance superstore, (xi) office supply store, or (xii) warehouse department store (e.g., Costco or Sams Club). As used in this Section 16.3, the term "Ongoing Co-Tenancy Requirement" shall mean that from and after the satisfaction of the Initial Co-Tenancy Requirement, at least three hundred thirty thousand (330,000) Leasable Square Feet in the Shopping Center (exclusive of the Premises) shall be open and continuously operated by retail tenants. If as of the Compliance Date the Initial Co-Tenancy Requirement is not satisfied, or if at any time thereafter the Ongoing Co-Tenancy Requirement is not satisfied, for so long as such non-satisfaction shall continue, Tenant shall have the right to terminate this Lease by not less than sixty (60) days', and not more than one hundred twenty (120) days', written notice delivered to Landlord prior to the date on which the Initial Co-Tenancy Requirement or the Ongoing Co-Tenancy Requirement, whichever is applicable, is satisfied. keyAssumptions: Source: JLL Offering Memorandum 'Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio' (99 pp., undated; cash flow 1/1/2027-12/31/2037). This property: overview PDF p.23, site plan p.24, trade area p.25, assumptions/opex p.26, RE taxes p.27, rent roll pp.28-30, cash flow p.31.
TIE-OUT (verified by script): roster SF 548,500 = OM GLA 548,500; occupied 547,823 SF + vacant 677 SF; occupancy 99.9%.
TIE-OUT: in-place base rent on the roster $6,006,678 vs OM rent-roll total $6,006,678; JLL Year-1 EGR $7,337,085 - OpEx $1,830,689 = NOI $5,506,396 (matches the portfolio summary, p.1).
TIE-OUT: 2 tax parcel(s) on the OM tax page sum to $904,797 vs the cash-flow RE tax line $904,796 (2026 assessment x millage grown 3%, net of 2% discount where shown).
WALT 7.6 yrs computed SF-weighted from lease expiries as of 1/1/2027 (OM states 7.6); weighted-avg base rent $10.96/SF over rent-paying occupied SF.
NO asking price or cap rate is disclosed (portfolio is marketed unpriced) - both left null.

JLL leasing assumptions: 75% renewal probability, 12 months downtime, $30/SF TI new / $0 renewal, 6%/3% LCs, 5% general vacancy (excluding credit/anchor tenants), 3% management fee, $0.20/SF reserves.

Lease-clause detail (co-tenancy, exclusives, termination/go-dark, ROFR) comes from the seller's summary workbook 'Midwest & Midatlantic Portfolio - Exclusives, Co-Tenancy, Restrictions.xlsx' - a summary, NOT the executed leases; every clause is marked unverified.
Rent roll as-of: OM cash flow starts 1/1/2027; tenantsAsOf set to that date by convention.
Roster: 547,823 SF leased + 677 SF vacant (suite 205) = 548,500 SF GLA; 99.9% occupied matches the OM.
Wayfair (94,847 SF) and its $853,623 are counted as occupied, matching the OM, but flagged as signed-not-open (lease start 1/1/2027, seller-paid costs).
Percentage rent: JLL Year-1 $15,099.
Target pays $3.43/SF on 127,466 SF to 1/31/2042 with three 15-yr options ($3.80, $4.18) - economically a ground lease.

Kuhn's lease tenant of record appears to be UNFI Wholesale, Inc. (seller clause workbook) - the UNFI row's ROFR on the Michaels space and its food/medical/office exclusive were mapped to Kuhn's; confirm.
UNFI/Kuhn's exclusive bars doctor/dentist/medical and business-office uses within 500 feet of its premises - check BioLife Plasma (13,357 SF) and Premier Imaging against it.

Tenant sales from the Gumberg 'Gross Sales History' report (Dec-2024 run; both files 'Pages 1-80' and 'Pages 81-138 from All Property Sales.pdf'); only full 12-month (or annual-filer) years are used - partial/catch-up years are skipped. Sales PSF uses the OM rent-roll SF.
deals.notes: **North Hills Village** is a **548,500 SF power center** on the McKnight Road/Route 19 corridor in Ross Township - the same node as Ross Park Mall - with the strongest demographics in the portfolio (**$116,817 AHHI within 3 miles**) and **5.0M annual visits (99th percentile)**. It is effectively **99.9% leased** (one 677 SF suite vacant) and throws off **$5,506,396 of Year-1 NOI**, but the OM's 'grocery anchor' is thin: **Kuhn's (53,000 SF, $11.00/SF) expires 3/31/2029 with NO options**, and Kuhn's lease is held by UNFI Wholesale per the seller's summary. The income is really the boxes - **Kohl's (93,000 SF, 18% of base rent) to 2/2029 with four flat $11.50 options, Best Buy (46,855 SF, $15.00) to 3/2028 with no options**, Michaels, Petco, Staples - plus **Target (127,466 SF) on a quasi-ground lease at $3.43/SF to 2042** with 15-year options. **Wayfair (94,847 SF, $853,623 = 14% of base rent) is a new lease that only starts 1/1/2027** with the seller paying the costs, so the largest single income line is not yet open. **2028-29 is the risk window: $3.03M (50%) of base rent rolls**, including two boxes (Best Buy, Kuhn's) with no options - genuine mark-to-market or vacancy events. JLL's tax line ($904,796) is also ~$210k below the 2024-25 actuals, which flatters expenses. Thesis: best-in-portfolio location and near-full occupancy, but a near-term re-tenanting story rather than a long-WALT grocery deal. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: **Best demographics in the portfolio ($116,817 AHHI)** and **99.9% leased**, offset by a **Kuhn's grocer with no options expiring 3/2029**, **Wayfair's $854k not yet open**, and **50% of base rent rolling in 2028-29**.
strengths: Highest-income trade area in the portfolio: $116,817 AHHI / 73,723 people within 3 miles; 206,394 within 5. Applebee's does $733/SF, Sally Beauty $313, Five Below $226, Petco $170 (11% rent-to-sales).
99.9% leased; 5.0M visits L12M - 99th percentile among U.S. shopping centers.
Credit box lineup: Target, Kohl's, Best Buy, Wayfair, Michaels, Petco, Staples, Five Below.
Target (127,466 SF) at $3.43/SF to 2042 + three 15-yr options - long, sticky, below-market income that anchors traffic.
Roster, base rent ($6,006,678) and tax parcels tie exactly to the OM; WALT 7.6 yrs matches the OM.
risks: Kuhn's (the only grocer) expires 3/31/2029 with no options - OM's 'grocery-anchored' framing depends on a renewal that isn't contracted.
Wayfair ($853,623, 14% of base rent) commences 1/1/2027 with seller-paid costs - not yet open and a newer big-box concept.
2028-29 rollover: Best Buy (no options), Kuhn's (no options), Kohl's, Michaels, Rally House, DXL, La Belle, GameStop - $3.03M (50% of base).
JLL proforma RE taxes $904,796 vs $1,099,125 (2024) and $1,115,167 (2025) actuals.
Sales are reported only for the smaller tenants (no Kohl's, Best Buy, Kuhn's, Target or Staples figures); Rally House runs 19.6% base rent-to-sales and Hong BBQ's last full year (2022) was $126/SF.

upsideItems.detail: Best Buy pays $15.00/SF on 46,855 SF with no options; JLL's 20,001-50,000 SF market rent is $17.00/SF - about $94k of lift if it renews at market, and the box is replaceable if it leaves.
No options remain; JLL's grocer market rent is $12.00/SF vs $11.00 in place - modest lift (~$53k) but, more importantly, the chance to lock a long-term grocer.

upsideItems.item: Michaels ROFR space / basement and second-floor space
upsideItems.detail: Wayfair holds a ROFO on Basement/Second-Floor space for 10 years, and Kuhn's (UNFI) holds a ROFR on the Michaels space - both constrain but also signal demand for expansion space.

redFlags.description: GROCER WITH NO OPTIONS - Kuhn's (53,000 SF, $583,000, 10% of base rent) expires 3/31/2029 with no options remaining; JLL simply 'assumes tenant renews at market'. The seller's summary shows the lease is in UNFI Wholesale's name. No Kuhn's sales were provided. Diligence the operator's intentions and store sales before paying for a grocery-anchored center.

2028-29 BOX ROLLOVER - Best Buy (46,855 SF, $702,825, 3/2028, NO options), Kohl's (93,000 SF, $1,069,500, 2/2029, four flat $11.50 options), Kuhn's (3/2029, NO options) and Michaels (6/2029) - with small-shop rolls, $3,026,996 (50%) of base rent expires in 2028-29.

WAYFAIR NOT YET OPEN - 94,847 SF at $9.00/SF ($853,623) commencing 1/1/2027 'with costs associated on the seller'. It is the second-largest rent line; confirm the lease is fully executed, the delivery/opening conditions, and that seller credits for TI/free rent are funded at closing.

TAX LINE BELOW ACTUALS - JLL carries $904,796 of RE taxes vs $1,461,794 (2023), $1,099,125 (2024) and $1,115,167 (2025) actuals (OM p.26). With ~73% recovery the net NOI effect is smaller, but the gross expense line is understated by ~$200k vs the 2025 actual - find out whether a successful appeal supports it.

keyAssumptions: Source: JLL Offering Memorandum 'Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio' (99 pp., undated; cash flow 1/1/2027-12/31/2037). This property: overview PDF p.33, site plan p.34, trade area p.35, assumptions/opex p.36, RE taxes p.37, rent roll pp.38-39, cash flow p.40.
TIE-OUT (verified by script): roster SF 134,974 = OM GLA 134,974; occupied 134,974 SF + vacant 0 SF; occupancy 100.0%.
TIE-OUT: in-place base rent on the roster $1,586,815 vs OM rent-roll total $1,586,815; JLL Year-1 EGR $2,054,463 - OpEx $555,380 = NOI $1,499,083 (matches the portfolio summary, p.1).
TIE-OUT: 8 tax parcel(s) on the OM tax page sum to $264,724 vs the cash-flow RE tax line $264,724 (2026 assessment x millage grown 3%, net of 2% discount where shown).
WALT 4.2 yrs computed SF-weighted from lease expiries as of 1/1/2027 (OM states 4.2); weighted-avg base rent $11.76/SF over rent-paying occupied SF.
NO asking price or cap rate is disclosed (portfolio is marketed unpriced) - both left null.

JLL leasing assumptions: 75% renewal probability, 12 months downtime, $30/SF TI new / $0 renewal, 6%/3% LCs, 5% general vacancy (excluding credit/anchor tenants), 3% management fee, $0.20/SF reserves.

Lease-clause detail (co-tenancy, exclusives, termination/go-dark, ROFR) comes from the seller's summary workbook 'Midwest & Midatlantic Portfolio - Exclusives, Co-Tenancy, Restrictions.xlsx' - a summary, NOT the executed leases; every clause is marked unverified.
Rent roll as-of: OM cash flow starts 1/1/2027; tenantsAsOf set to that date by convention.
Address: OM p.33 property summary shows 8901 US-30; the portfolio map (p.2) shows 8931 US-30 - used the property-summary address.
Target row on the rent roll is a NAP (non-owned) parcel contributing to CAM (agreement 1/1/2026 - 1/19/2055); carried as isNAP with 0 SF, so it does not affect GLA or occupancy.

Giant Eagle sales: OM states $77,553,436 / $749 PSF (p.3, p.33); the Gumberg report shows CY2023 $76,425,930 ($738/SF) and Jan-Sep 2024 running ~2.6% ahead of Jan-Sep 2023. Percentage-rent breakpoint $95,179,029 at 1% - not in overage.
Other sales (Gumberg report, bldg 523): Firepit $519/SF (CY2023, 2.6% rent-to-sales), Famous Footwear $217/SF (CY2024, 9.7%).

Tenant sales from the Gumberg 'Gross Sales History' report (Dec-2024 run; both files 'Pages 1-80' and 'Pages 81-138 from All Property Sales.pdf'); only full 12-month (or annual-filer) years are used - partial/catch-up years are skipped. Sales PSF uses the OM rent-roll SF.
deals.notes: **North Huntingdon Square** is a **134,974 SF, 100%-leased Giant Eagle-anchored center** on Route 30 (+25,000 VPD) directly adjacent to the PA Turnpike (I-76, +50,000 VPD) in Westmoreland County, with **$111,741 AHHI within 3 miles** and 4.5M annual visits. It is essentially a **Giant Eagle net-lease investment**: the 103,541 SF store pays **$1,054,047 (66% of base rent)** at $10.18/SF and does an exceptional **$77.55M ($749/SF) - a 1.4% rent-to-sales ratio**, with four 5-year options at $10.68-$12.18. Target (A) owns its own parcel next door (NAP, contributes to CAM) and Kohl's is a shadow anchor, so the center captures traffic it doesn't pay for. The balance is pads and small boxes - Panera, Famous Footwear, Bob Evans, Eat'n Park, Firepit, Valvoline, GetGo - most separately parcelled, giving a **pad spin-off option**. Year-1 NOI is **$1,499,083** with a 4.2-year WALT, and growth is minimal (JLL Yr1-6 NOI CAGR 1.4%). The one real risk is concentration: **72% of base rent expires in 2030** (Giant Eagle 11/2030, Firepit, GetGo), but with $749/SF sales and below-market fixed options the Giant Eagle renewal is about as safe as grocery income gets. Thesis: bond-like, grocer-dominated cash flow with pad-sale optionality. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: A **100%-leased Giant Eagle doing $77.55M ($749/SF, 1.4% rent-to-sales)** with Target/Kohl's shadow traffic - bond-like income whose only real risk is **72% of base rent expiring in 2030** behind a near-certain Giant Eagle renewal.
strengths: Giant Eagle sales of $77,553,436 ($749/SF) at 1.4% rent-to-sales - one of the healthiest grocer ratios in the database; four fixed options to 2050.
100% leased; Target (S&P A, NAP parcel, contributes to CAM) and Kohl's shadow-anchor the site.
I-76 / Route 30 adjacency with four points of ingress/egress; $111,741 AHHI within 3 miles.
Separately parcelled pads (Bob Evans, Eat'n Park, Valvoline, Panera) support a pad-sale program.
Clean tie-out: roster 134,974 SF = GLA; base $1,586,815 = roll; 8 tax parcels sum to the $264,724 tax line.
risks: Giant Eagle = 66% of base rent; 72% of base rent expires in 2030 (Giant Eagle 11/2030, Firepit, GetGo).
Flat growth: JLL Yr1-6 NOI CAGR 1.4%; Giant Eagle's option bumps are ~5% per 5 years.
Famous Footwear (8% of base rent) and Firepit have no options; Eat'n Park's only option is flat at $17.02.
No co-tenancy/clause detail for Giant Eagle beyond its go-dark recapture right; no sales for the in-line/pad tenants.

upsideItems.detail: Bob Evans (S&P B+, 2.7 yrs), Valvoline (9.4 yrs), Eat'n Park and Panera sit on separate tax parcels; selling 2-3 pads at STNL cap rates could return a meaningful slice of basis (OM p.33 calls this out).
Both have no options (6/2031 and 11/2030); JLL in-line market rent is $22.00/SF vs $20.90 and $13.71 in place - Firepit is the real gap (~$45k).

redFlags.description: SINGLE-TENANT CONCENTRATION - Giant Eagle is 103,541 SF (76.7% of GLA) and $1,054,047 (66%) of base rent, expiring 11/30/2030. Its sales ($749/SF) make renewal very likely, but this is credit/renewal concentration that should be priced like a net-lease grocer.
2030-31 ROLLOVER - Giant Eagle, Firepit and GetGo (11/2030) plus Famous Footwear and Eat'n Park (2031) = 86% of base rent inside ~5 years; Famous Footwear and Firepit have no options.

deals.shadowAnchors: Target (127,000+ SF, owner-occupied NAP parcel that contributes to CAM; ~1.2M visits L12M, S&P A) and Kohl's (shadow anchor, ~572,600 visits L12M).

exclusiveUse.verbatimQuote: Landlord shall not use or allow any other person or entity (except Tenant) to use any portion of the Property for the sale of: (a) whole or ground coffee beans, (b) espresso, espresso-based drinks or coffee-based drinks, (c) tea or tea-based drinks, (d) brewed coffee or (e) blended beverages similar to Starbucks Frappuccino®. Notwithstanding the foregoing sentence, other tenants may sell non-gourmet, non-brand identified brewed coffee or brewed tea. For purposes of this Lease, "gourmet" shall be defined as: (a) beverages made using Arabica beans or (b) sourced from a gourmet coffee brand such as Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf, Intelligentsia, Peets, Caribou or other coffee purveyor. For purposes of this Lease, "brand identified" shall mean beverages advertised or marketed within the applicable retail space using a brand name or served in a brand-identified cup. In addition, other tenants may sell pre-bottled tea or pre-bottled tea-based beverages. Fast food restaurants such as Wendy's, McDonald's, and Burger King may sell brewed coffee or tea for on-premises consumption or for take out. Landlord shall not lease space to a bakery-style restaurant that has an espresso bar.

deals.notes: **Eastgate Shopping Center** is a **274,460 SF Giant Eagle-anchored neighborhood center** on Route 30 (20,000+ VPD) in Greensburg, the Westmoreland County seat, with **$96,415 AHHI within 3 miles** and 2.8M annual visits (#1 neighborhood center within 10 miles). It is **98.0% leased** with **$2,555,775 of Year-1 NOI**. Giant Eagle (88,147 SF, $9.35/SF, 29% of base rent) has the **longest anchor term in the portfolio - to 12/31/2035** with a step to $10.06 in 2031 and two options - and does **$38.75M ($440/SF, 2.1% rent-to-sales)**, lower volume than the Pittsburgh stores but stable (CY2024 $39.0M). The second-largest rent line is unusual: **Biscotti Brothers bakery in 62,061 SF at $4.95/SF (11%)** to 10/2030, plus **Smail Auto Group on 23,494 SF at $1.11/SF** - low-value space that dilutes the average rent ($10.56). The pad ring is high quality - Chick-fil-A, Starbucks, PNC, 1st Summit Bank, Sleep Number, Tropical Bungalow - and the OM pitches **pad spin-offs**. Rollover is granular (11% in 2027, led by Dollar General with one option), recoveries are low (53% of opex), and growth is modest (JLL Yr1-6 NOI CAGR 2.3%). Thesis: a long-term grocer with nine years of term and a sellable pad ring - steady cash flow rather than a value-add story. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: **Giant Eagle locked to 12/31/2035** (longest anchor term in the portfolio) with **$440/SF sales** and a **sellable pad ring**, tempered by low-value secondary space (**Biscotti 62,061 SF at $4.95; Smail Auto at $1.11**) and only 53% expense recovery.
strengths: Giant Eagle to 12/31/2035 + two options; $38.75M sales at 2.1% rent-to-sales, flat-to-up since 2020.
98.0% leased; 2.8M visits, #1 neighborhood center within 10 miles.
Quality pads: Chick-fil-A, Starbucks (S&P BBB+), PNC, 1st Summit Bank ($53.88/SF), Sleep Number, Tropical Bungalow.
Granular in-line rollover - no single year above 14% of base rent through 2031.
Roster, rent ($2,839,187) and tax parcels tie exactly.
risks: Biscotti Brothers 62,061 SF at $4.95/SF (11% of rent, 10/2030) and Smail Auto 23,494 SF at $1.11/SF - large, low-value space.
Low expense recovery (53% of opex) leaves the landlord carrying most cost growth.
Dollar General (18,782 SF) expires 10/31/2027 with one option; DG's 2024 sales reporting is incomplete (last clean year CY2022 $107/SF).
Cosmoprof and Starbucks have Giant Eagle co-tenancy (termination / 50% rent) - harmless today but tied to the anchor.

upsideItems.detail: Chick-fil-A, Starbucks, PNC, 1st Summit, Sleep Number and Tropical Bungalow pay $20-$54/SF on separate tax parcels; selling 2-3 pads at STNL pricing is the OM's stated value-add (p.42).
Four small suites (563-3,352 SF, three on the 2nd floor) at JLL's $10-$27/SF - ~$60-90k of rent; small but low-cost.

redFlags.description: SECONDARY SPACE - Biscotti Brothers (62,061 SF, 22.6% of GLA) at $4.95/SF and Smail Auto Group (23,494 SF) at $1.11/SF together occupy 31% of the GLA for 12% of base rent. Understand what this space physically is (the site plan shows a 2nd-floor/rear component) before valuing it as retail.

DOLLAR GENERAL 2027 EXPIRY - 18,782 SF / $109,593 expiring 10/31/2027 with one option at $6.31/SF; Dollar General has been closing stores. The landlord holds a recapture right if DG goes dark 30 days.

deals.notes: **Hermitage Towne Plaza** is a **379,377 SF Giant Eagle-anchored community center** on E. State Street in Hermitage (Mercer County, Shenango Valley), the #2 most-visited center within 10 miles (2.6M visits). It is **93.5% leased** with **$2,670,396 of Year-1 NOI** and the lowest average rent of the PA assets (**$8.71/SF**). Giant Eagle (74,930 SF, $8.50/SF) does **$53.55M ($715/SF, 1.2% rent-to-sales)** - the #1 Giant Eagle within 30 miles - with term to 11/2033 and two options, and the box roster has been aggressively re-tenanted out of distress: **Big Lots -> Ross (36,480 SF, opening 1/1/2027)** and **Jo-Ann -> Michaels (2025)**, alongside Gabe's, T.J. Maxx ($322/SF sales), Ollie's, Dunham's and Shoe Show. That churn is the key diligence point: **$335,054 of rent (Ross, Dubz Grill, 7 Brew) only starts at the 1/1/2027 analysis start with seller-paid costs**, and **Gabe's co-tenancy is keyed to Big Lots** - with Big Lots closed and Ross not yet open, Gabe's may already be entitled to a 50% abatement. Demographics are the weakest of the PA centers (**$80,795 AHHI, 24,815 people within 3 miles**), which argues for cap-rate cushion. JLL projects 5.1% NOI CAGR from lease-up of the 24,500 SF vacancy and the new leases. Thesis: a dominant grocer in a thin secondary market, with income that is newly re-tenanted rather than seasoned. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: A **$53.5M ($715/SF) Giant Eagle** to 2033 and a freshly re-tenanted box lineup, discounted for a **thin trade area ($80,795 AHHI)**, **$335k of rent not yet open**, and **Gabe's Big Lots co-tenancy possibly in effect**.
strengths: Giant Eagle $53.5M sales ($715/SF, 1.2% rent-to-sales) - #1 Giant Eagle within 30 miles; term to 11/2033 + two options.
Distressed boxes already backfilled with stronger credits: Big Lots -> Ross, Jo-Ann -> Michaels (2025, three options, $17.75/SF).
Healthy box sales: T.J. Maxx $322/SF (2.0% rent-to-sales), Pet Supplies Plus $338, Bath & Body Works $583, Great China Wok $386.
OM: 53% of gross income from leases signed since 2020.
Roster and rent ($3,089,803) tie exactly to the OM.
risks: Thin trade area: $80,795 AHHI and 24,815 people within 3 miles.
$335,054 of rent (Ross $214,500, Dubz Grill $50,554, 7 Brew $70,000) commences 1/1/2027 with seller-paid costs.
Gabe's co-tenancy requires Giant Eagle AND Big Lots (or replacement) open - 50% abatement after 180 days.
2027 rollover 13% (Ollie's 11/2027, Bath & Body Works 1/2027, Great Clips, Cricket, Hunger Station, Kraynak's); 2030 rollover 19% (Gabe's, Dunham's, Shoe Show - two with no options).
Shoe Show Mega does only $39/SF on 27,468 SF; Dunham's $148/SF - both with no options.

upsideItems.detail: JLL's 20,001-40,000 SF market rent is $8.00/SF - ~$196k of base rent (JLL's Yr-1 absorption deduction is exactly this), ~7% of NOI.

Shoe Show (27,468 SF at $3.13, $39/SF sales) and Dunham's (21,600 SF at $4.91) expire 2/2030 and 1/2030 with no options; JLL's market for 20-40k SF is $8.00/SF - backfilling either at market adds ~$65-$135k.

redFlags.description: GABE'S CO-TENANCY MAY BE TRIPPED NOW - Gabe's (49,999 SF, $259,995) requires Giant Eagle AND Big Lots (or a >=10-store replacement) open; after 180 days it gets 50% abatement of ALL sums, and after 18 more months must terminate or revert. Big Lots' last sales in the Gumberg report are 2024; Ross does not open until ~1/1/2027. The OM shows Gabe's at full rent - get the Gabe's estoppel and a seller rep.

INCOME NOT YET OPEN - Ross ($214,500), Dubz Grill ($50,554) and 7 Brew ($70,000) all start 1/1/2027 'with costs associated on the seller' - $335,054 (12.5% of NOI). Confirm executed leases, delivery conditions, and that TI/LC/free rent are credited at closing.

WEAK TRADE AREA - 24,815 people and $80,795 AHHI within 3 miles (79,307 within 10); the Placer trade area is 112,980 people over 181 sq mi. Below-portfolio demographics argue for more cap-rate cushion and conservative rent growth.

goDarkRight.verbatimQuote: Tenant shall be required to open for business to the public (as a Harbor Freight Tools retail store) for at least one (1) day within 180 days from the Rent Commencement Date ("Outside Opening Date"). Landlord shall have, as its sole and exclusive remedy for Tenant's failure to open by the Outside Opening Date, the right (by providing Tenant with sixty (60) days written notice) to terminate this Lease at any time after the Outside Opening Date, but prior to the date Tenant opens the Premises for business to the public (provided, further, that Landlord's termination right shall be null and void if Tenant then opens for business to the public during the thirty (30) day period following receipt of the notice). After Tenant satisfies the one (1) day opening obligation set forth herein, Tenant shall have no obligation to continuously operate at the Premises. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in In the event that Tenant shall discontinue the operation of Tenant's business in the Premises for a period of at least 180 consecutive days (unless due to casualty, Condemnation, repair, remodeling, transitioning an assignee or sublessee, Force Majeure, or as otherwise expressly permitted under this Lease), Landlord may, as its sole remedy, upon 60 days written notice to Tenant, terminate this Lease; provided, however, that Tenant may nullify such termination by reopening for business in the Premises within thirty (30) days of receipt of Landlord's termination notice.

deals.notes: **Chillicothe Shopping Center** is a **305,078 SF community center** (a former enclosed mall with JCPenney) on N Bridge Street / Route 23 (+27,500 VPD) in Chillicothe, OH, 45 miles south of Columbus - the #1 most-visited center within 15 miles (3.6M visits) but in a **thin, lower-income trade area ($74,775 AHHI, 26,098 people within 3 miles)**. It is **90.4% leased** with **$1,716,643 of Year-1 NOI** and a **2.9-year WALT - the shortest in the portfolio**. The 'grocery anchor' is **Aldi (19,923 SF, 8% of base rent)** - a good credit with term to 2036, but too small to anchor 305,000 SF. The real anchor is **JCPenney (68,787 SF at $3.49/SF), expiring 12/31/2027 with sales of only $5.18M ($75/SF) and falling** - and JCPenney is written into the co-tenancy of Bath & Body Works, Kay, Maurices and T.J. Maxx. Those in-line tenants are strong (**T.J. Maxx $541/SF, Bath & Body Works $783, Kay $648**), which is the asset's best feature. **38% of base rent rolls in 2027-28** and **29,277 SF of vacancy** sits in six mall-interior suites; JLL's 6.0% NOI CAGR depends on leasing it ($652k of TI in Year 2). Thesis: a value-add/re-tenanting play priced off a short, JCPenney-dependent rent roll, not a stabilized grocery center. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: **Strong in-line sales (T.J. Maxx $541/SF, BBW $783)** can't offset a **2.9-year WALT**, a **$75/SF JCPenney expiring 12/2027** that four tenants' co-tenancy hangs on, and a **thin trade area ($74,775 AHHI)** behind an Aldi too small to anchor the center.
strengths: Productive national in-line tenants: T.J. Maxx $541/SF (1.6% rent-to-sales), Bath & Body Works $783, Kay $648, Crumbl $503.
#1 most-visited center within 15 miles; Route 23 frontage (+27,500 VPD).
Aldi to 10/31/2036 with five options; Harbor Freight with five options; Dunham's with four.
Roster and rent ($2,064,461) tie exactly; OM 90% occupancy confirmed (90.4%).
risks: 2.9-year WALT; 38% of base rent expires in 2027-28 (JCPenney, McDonald's, Harbor Freight, Dollar Tree, Crumbl, Boba Tea, HoneyBaked).
JCPenney: 68,787 SF, $75/SF sales (down from $82), expiring 12/31/2027 with two FLAT options at $3.49.
JCPenney co-tenancy dependents: Bath & Body Works (termination / alternative rent), Kay (3% of sales), Maurices (termination), T.J. Maxx (alternate rent).
29,277 SF of vacancy in six interior suites; JLL Year-2 TI $651,810 and LC $212,955.
Low recoveries (38% of opex).

upsideItems.detail: Six suites (800-8,327 SF) at JLL's $12-$20/SF - roughly $350-450k of rent if fully leased, ~20-25% of NOI; but it is mall-interior space and JLL budgets $652k of TI to get there.
If JCPenney leaves in 2027, 68,787 SF at $3.49 is deeply below JLL's $6.00/SF (50k+) market and could be demised for boxes - an exit-value lever, but also the main risk.

Maxx ($218,750) all have co-tenancy tied to JCPenney - a JCP closure puts ~$510k of in-line rent at risk on top of JCP's own $240,067.

THIN TRADE AREA - $74,775 AHHI and 26,098 people within 3 miles (57,451 within 10). Rent growth and backfill rents should be underwritten conservatively.

coTenancy.verbatimQuote: "Co-Tenancy Violation" shall exist when during the Term, less than fifty percent 50% of the leasable area of all buildings comprising the Shopping Center is occupied by tenants open and operating for business to the public, except where due to fire, casualty or condemnation or Force Majeure event. If a Co-Tenancy Violation exists and continues for a period of 60 days, then, Tenant's Base Rent due hereunder shall decrease to 50% of the Base Rent. Further, if the Co-tenancy Violation exists for a period of 12 consecutive months, at any time thereafter, Tenant shall have the right to terminate this Lease upon 60 days prior written notice to Landlord. If at any time, the Co-tenancy Violation ceases to exist, Tenant's Base Rent shall be restored to the full amount due pursuant to Section 3.1 of this Lease and Tenant shall no longer have the right to terminate this Lease. Further, if Tenant does not elect to terminate this Lease within 30 days after the aforesaid 12 month period, then Tenant's Base Rent shall be restored to the full amount due pursuant to Section 3.1 of this Lease effective the first day after the aforesaid 12 month period.

keyAssumptions: Source: JLL Offering Memorandum 'Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio' (99 pp., undated; cash flow 1/1/2027-12/31/2037). This property: overview PDF p.73, site plan p.74, trade area p.75, assumptions/opex p.76, RE taxes p.77-78, rent roll pp.79-84, cash flow p.85.
TIE-OUT (verified by script): roster SF 388,143 = OM GLA 388,143; occupied 358,520 SF + vacant 29,623 SF; occupancy 92.4%.
TIE-OUT: in-place base rent on the roster $2,607,613 vs OM rent-roll total $2,607,613; JLL Year-1 EGR $2,983,669 - OpEx $1,112,420 = NOI $1,871,250 (matches the portfolio summary, p.1).
TIE-OUT: 12 tax parcel(s) on the OM tax page sum to $322,076 vs the cash-flow RE tax line $322,078 (2026 assessment x millage grown 3%, net of 2% discount where shown).
WALT 4.3 yrs computed SF-weighted from lease expiries as of 1/1/2027 (OM states 4.3); weighted-avg base rent $7.38/SF over rent-paying occupied SF.
NO asking price or cap rate is disclosed (portfolio is marketed unpriced) - both left null.

JLL leasing assumptions: 75% renewal probability, 12 months downtime, $30/SF TI new / $0 renewal, 6%/3% LCs, 5% general vacancy (excluding credit/anchor tenants), 3% management fee, $0.20/SF reserves.

Lease-clause detail (co-tenancy, exclusives, termination/go-dark, ROFR) comes from the seller's summary workbook 'Midwest & Midatlantic Portfolio - Exclusives, Co-Tenancy, Restrictions.xlsx' - a summary, NOT the executed leases; every clause is marked unverified.
Rent roll as-of: OM cash flow starts 1/1/2027; tenantsAsOf set to that date by convention.
Occupancy: 358,520 SF leased / 388,143 SF = 92.4% (OM 92%); Ross (25,299 SF) and Chick-fil-A (6,697 SF) counted as leased (signed-not-open).
Maurices (5,309 SF) has no fixed base rent - pays 8% of gross sales in lieu of rent; carried with $0 base rent.
Huntington ATM: 6 SF at $7,800/yr ($1,300/SF) - arithmetic, not comparable rent.
Mall-74 vacant suite shows JLL lease-up dates of 2110-2120 on the OM rent roll (typo) - dates ignored.
Percentage rent JLL Year-1 $100,965; other revenue $16,500.

Sales from the Gumberg report (bldgs 531 mall / 532 strip, CY2024 unless noted): Burger King $630/SF, Bath & Body Works $546, Hot Rice $505 (2023), Pet Supplies Plus $295, Rent-A-Center $262, Advance Auto $197, Dunham's $151, Shoe Dept $126, Maurices $95 ($504k - at 8% that is ~$40k/yr of percentage rent in lieu of base), Ollie's $71/SF (7.0% rent-to-sales). Phoenix Theatres' predecessor (Northtowne Cinema) fell to $355k of sales in 2023 before the 2023 re-lease.

Tenant sales from the Gumberg 'Gross Sales History' report (Dec-2024 run; both files 'Pages 1-80' and 'Pages 81-138 from All Property Sales.pdf'); only full 12-month (or annual-filer) years are used - partial/catch-up years are skipped. Sales PSF uses the OM rent-roll SF.
deals.notes: **Northtowne Shopping Center** is a **388,143 SF community center - the former Northtowne Mall plus an adjacent strip -** on N Clinton Street / Route 24 (+18,000 VPD) in Defiance, OH, shadow-anchored by a **Walmart Supercenter** (#1 Walmart within 30 miles). It is **92.4% leased** (including Ross and Chick-fil-A, which only start 1/1/2027) with **$1,871,250 of Year-1 NOI** at a low **$7.38/SF average rent**. The tenancy is box-heavy and value-oriented - Ollie's, Hobby Lobby, Marshalls, Dunham's, Family Farm & Home, Phoenix Theatres, Planet Fitness - plus **Xperience Church in 45,000 SF at $3.54/SF (lease to 3/2027)**. The structural problem is the **enclosed-mall interior: ~29,600 SF of vacancy spread across 20 small suites (462-5,864 SF)**, and an expense load the tenants barely cover - **recoveries are only 23% of opex** because most leases are gross/excluded. JLL's headline **'+56% NOI growth / 9.2% CAGR'** (OM p.73) is almost entirely lease-up and re-tenanting assumptions (Year-2 TI+LC $995k), not contractual. Co-tenancy is thin: **Maurices already pays 8% of sales in lieu of rent** (its JCPenney/Elder-Beerman anchors are gone) and **Marshalls' clause now rests on Hobby Lobby alone**. Demographics are small (**16,960 people within 3 miles**). Thesis: a deep value-add, small-market dead-mall repositioning - price it on in-place NOI, not JLL's lease-up. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: A **dead-mall repositioning in a 17k-person 3-mile market**: **~29,600 SF of fragmented interior vacancy**, **23% expense recovery**, a JLL **+56% NOI growth** case that is almost all lease-up, and co-tenancy that already **lost JCPenney** (Maurices on % rent; Marshalls hinging on Hobby Lobby).
strengths: Walmart Supercenter shadow anchor (#1 Walmart within 30 miles, 2.3M visits).
Healthy pad/strip sales: Burger King $630/SF, Bath & Body Works $546, Pet Supplies Plus $295, Rent-A-Center $262.
Value-oriented national box roster: Ollie's, Hobby Lobby, Marshalls, Ross (new), Dunham's, Family Farm & Home, Phoenix Theatres (to 2037), Planet Fitness.
Newer pads: 7Brew (2026, $75,000/yr), Take 5 (2025), Chick-fil-A (2027 ground lease).
Roster, rent ($2,607,613) and tax parcels tie exactly; OM 92% occupancy confirmed (92.4%).
risks: Enclosed-mall interior: ~29,600 SF vacant across 20 suites (462-5,864 SF).
Recoveries only $258,591 against $1,112,420 of opex (23%); NOI margin 63%.
JLL growth case (+56% NOI in 5 yrs) is lease-up driven; Year-2 TI $612,664 + LC $382,126.
Ollie's (47,495 SF, 9% of base rent, 7/2028) reports only $71/SF; Maurices ~$95/SF.
Xperience Church (45,000 SF, $3.54/SF) expires 3/31/2027 (four 3-yr options); a church is not a retail draw.
2027-28 rollover: $868,595 (33%) of base rent - Xperience, Ollie's, Dunham's, Advance Auto, Great Clips (master lease expiring), Shoe Dept, Maurices.
Taxes: JLL $322,078 vs $207,282 (2025 actual) - a 55% jump.

upsideItems.detail: At JLL's own interior rates ($10k-$30k/yr per small suite, $17-$20/SF for 1-10k SF) full lease-up is worth ~$664k - exactly JLL's Year-1 absorption-vacancy line - but 20 fragmented suites in a 17k-person 3-mile market likely need capital to de-mall or re-face the interior.
Burger King, 7Brew, Take 5, Arby's, State Bank and Chick-fil-A pads are separately parcelled; the OM cites a strong STNL submarket.

redFlags.description: INTERIOR-MALL VACANCY / OPERATING COST - ~29,600 SF of vacancy in 20 small interior suites plus an enclosed-mall cost structure: $532,783 of CAM and only $258,591 of total recoveries (23% of $1.11M opex). Small-shop demand in a 17k-person 3-mile radius is the question JLL's lease-up case doesn't answer.

CO-TENANCY ALREADY LOST ITS ANCHORS - Maurices' JCPenney/Elder-Beerman clause appears triggered (both gone) and it pays 8% of gross sales in lieu of base rent (to 1/2028). Marshalls (22,427 SF, $185,023) needs 2 of 3 of JCPenney / Hobby Lobby (>=51k SF) / a >=30k-SF national - with JCPenney gone, Hobby Lobby (lease to 8/2029) going dark ALONE trips it.

AGGRESSIVE PROJECTION - OM p.73 markets '+56% NOI growth & +9.2% CAGR on a 5-year hold'; JLL's Year-1 NOI is $1,871,250 rising to $2,418,353 in Year 2, driven by absorption of vacancy, not contractual rent. Underwrite on in-place NOI.
TAX LINE UP 55% - JLL carries $322,078 of RE taxes vs $207,282 (2025) actual (OM p.76) - likely a reassessment/millage update; with low recoveries most of it lands on NOI. Confirm the basis.

INCOME NOT YET OPEN - Ross ($145,469) and Chick-fil-A ($31,250, rising to $125k by 2029) start 1/1/2027 with seller-paid costs - $176,719. Great Clips sits on a master lease 'set to expire Oct-26' with direct deals out to Great Clips, Cricket and a smoke shop (OM rent-roll note).

deals.notes: **West Towne Center** is a **152,180 SF Home Depot-anchored center** on the Glenway Avenue corridor in Cincinnati's infill Western Hills submarket, 6.4 miles from downtown, with **96,162 people and $91,202 AHHI within 3 miles** (683,343 within 10). It is **88.5% leased** with **$805,149 of Year-1 NOI**, and is functionally a **Home Depot net-lease investment: Home Depot (S&P A) occupies 112,000 SF at $6.92/SF, $775,040 = 80% of base rent, to 1/31/2034** with one option at $7.81 and a 1-mile home-improvement exclusive. The balance is Fisher Auto Parts (16,684 SF, new 9/2025 lease at $7.00), a Bob Evans pad (12/2028, two options) and a Dillard's NAP parcel that contributes to CAM. The value-add is **the 17,500 SF vacant box (19B)** - formerly Cincinnati Open Box Outlet - which JLL leases from 7/2028 at $9.25/SF after $525k of TI. Real estate taxes are heavy (**$261,065, 32% of NOI**) and Ohio school boards routinely challenge values after a sale. Thesis: long-dated A-credit Home Depot income at a low rent basis, with modest box lease-up upside. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

deals.notes: **Waverly Plaza** is a **219,629 SF Home Depot-anchored center** at S. Waverly Road and St. Joe Highway in Delta Township (Lansing, MI), near I-496 (+50,000 VPD), with a 10-mile population of 315,267 but the **lowest 3-mile income in the portfolio ($73,228 AHHI)**. It is **85.0% leased** with **$1,165,644 of Year-1 NOI**. **Home Depot (113,260 SF at $7.46/SF) is 63% of base rent to 1/31/2033** with two options (to $9.03) and a 1-mile home-improvement exclusive; the rest is **Ollie's (37,000 SF, $6.01, $129/SF sales, one option)**, **Defy (trampoline park, 33,350 SF at $6.60, no options, 4/2031)** and a Tim Hortons pad that has been there since 1985. The value-add is the **32,811 SF vacant box (suite 12)**, which JLL leases from 1/2029 at $10.00/SF - that one box is most of JLL's 7.2% NOI CAGR. The key tax issue is Michigan-specific: **property taxes are only $91,426** because taxable value is capped, and **a sale 'uncaps' taxable value to 50% of market value** - a near-certain step-up that this OM does not model, and Home Depot's recovery code shows taxes EXCLUDED. Thesis: low-basis Home Depot income with one big lease-up, priced net of a post-sale tax reset. Part of JLL's **9-property, 3,027,794 SF Midwest & Mid-Atlantic Grocery-Anchored Portfolio** (portfolio Year-1 NOI $28,370,304), offered **unpriced** - no asking price or cap rate is disclosed for the portfolio or any asset.

dealScore.rationale: **Home Depot (63% of rent) to 2033** at a **$7.15/SF** average with a **32,811 SF box to lease**, offset by **85% occupancy**, the **portfolio's lowest 3-mile income ($73,228)** and a **Michigan tax uncapping on sale** the OM doesn't model.
strengths: Home Depot to 1/31/2033 + two options; #1 Home Depot within 30 miles (1.2M center visits); 1-mile home-improvement exclusive.
Low rent basis ($7.15/SF average on occupied space).
I-496 / Lansing MSA location with 315,267 people within 10 miles; Lansing Mall and GM Delta Township Assembly nearby.

risks: 15% vacancy: 32,811 SF box (suite 12) plus a 128 SF static ATM vacancy.

2031 rollover: Ollie's (1/2031, one option) and Defy (4/2031, no options) = 33% of base rent.

redFlags.description: MICHIGAN TAX UNCAPPING ON SALE - taxes are only $91,426 on 219,629 SF ($0.42/SF). In Michigan a transfer of ownership uncaps taxable value to the State Equalized Value (50% of true cash value), so the post-sale bill is likely to step up materially. JLL grows the current bill at 3%. Home Depot's reimbursement code shows RE taxes EXCLUDED - confirm whether Home Depot pays its own parcel's taxes directly before sizing the hit.
